$comment: THE hand-written part. Four packages -- ui, js, php, py -- are generated from this directory and are never edited. Every fact here is read from Google's own discovery document (https://gmail.googleapis.com/$discovery/rest?version=v1), not from docs prose.
title: Gmail

oauth.$refreshTokenRotates: Reusable. A refresh response carries access_token, expires_in, scope and token_type — no refresh_token — and Google’s own expiry rule is "the refresh token has not been used for six months", which is a statement about a token that is PERSISTED AND REPLAYED. Under rotation it would change hourly and that rule could never fire.
oauth.$grantComment: ONE consent grant shared by every Google connector (MOIC #1, 2026-11-08). A host may run them all on one OAuth client: request each feature's scopes when it is first used, with include_granted_scopes=true, and Google's new token covers every scope granted before. A refresh token comes back only on the FIRST code exchange with access_type=offline, so keep the stored one when an exchange returns none. Revoking ANY token removes the person's WHOLE grant -- every Google connector, not this one -- so a per-feature disconnect stops using the scope locally and only a full Google disconnect revokes. Identify the account by the id_token's sub (request openid; verify iss and aud = clientId), never by email.
oauth.$restrictedScopesComment: Google's RESTRICTED tier puts the whole OAuth client under verification and an annual CASA assessment. None of this connector's scopes is restricted.
oauth.$scopeComment: gmail.send, which is the NARROWEST scope that can send. The discovery document lists https://mail.google.com/ first for this method -- full read, write and delete over the entire mailbox -- and taking the first entry would grant an automation the ability to delete somebody's mail in order to send one message. gmail.send cannot read a single message.
oauth.$comment: The package DECLARES the dance and does not perform it. Google's access tokens last ONE HOUR, so refreshToken is required rather than optional -- and Google only issues one when the consent request asked for offline access.

$sandboxComment: CHECKED. Gmail has no test estate: there is one API and a test mailbox is a real mailbox. Anything this action sends is delivered for real, to a real person.
sandboxNote: Gmail has no sandbox. A send is a real email to a real address -- point this at your own inbox before pointing it at anybody else's. The faker is the only way to develop against it without delivering mail.
summary: Send Gmail messages from a workflow or a Laravel app, as the connected Google account.
$setupComment: Steps read from Google's docs on 2026-11-14 (each cites its page). Every Google connector shares one grant, so the first four steps are the same for all of them; do them once.

setup.title: Create (or reuse) the Google Cloud project for {{appName}}
setup.detail: Every Google connector shares ONE consent grant (oauth.grant "google"), so use one project and one OAuth client for all of them: one consent and one refresh token per person.

setup.title: Enable the Gmail API
setup.detail: Console: APIs & Services, Library; open the Gmail API and click Enable.

setup.title: Configure the consent screen
setup.detail: Console: Google Auth platform, Branding (app name {{appName}}, support email, contact email), then Audience: Internal for people inside your Google Workspace organisation only, or External (while it is in testing, add each tester under Test users). Then Data Access, Add or Remove Scopes, and add `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/gmail.send` beside the scopes of any other Google connector you use. You cannot remove the consent screen once it is configured.

setup.title: Create a Web application OAuth client
setup.detail: Console: Google Auth platform, Clients, Create Client; type Web application. Under Authorized redirect URIs click Add URI and paste {{oauthRedirectUrl}}, then Create. Copy the client ID and client secret when the client is created.

setup.title: Connect an account and check it works
setup.detail: Connect one Google account through {{appName}}'s OAuth flow, then run the check below.
setup.prompt: Using {{appName}}'s {{connector}} connection, send one message with message_send to the connected account's OWN address, subject "{{appName}} setup check", and report the returned message id.
setup.done: message_send returns an id and the message arrives in the account's own inbox.

credentialFields.label: OAuth client ID
credentialFields.help: From Google Cloud Console -> APIs & Services -> Credentials. ONE value for the whole installation, not per connected account.

credentialFields.label: OAuth client secret
credentialFields.help: The client secret for the same OAuth app. One value for the whole installation.

credentialFields.label: Access token
credentialFields.help: Per connected Google account, and it expires after ONE HOUR. The host refreshes it with the refresh token.

credentialFields.label: Refresh token
credentialFields.help: Per connected Google account. Google issues one only when the consent request asks for offline access; without it the connection dies within the hour.
